title: Ask parent's real Move execution path materially widens sparse-population company-name searches beyond the specialist's own certified contract
owningRepoBestGuess: savitz25/Move-trust-Hub (the /api/specialist-execution/v2 handler specifically) -- inferred from black-box behavior, NOT confirmed by reading Move-trust-Hub's source (no local clone; read-only per spec)
exactReproduction: 1) GET https://www.movetrusthub.com/api/ask?q=JK+Moving+Services -> terminalState=NEEDS_CLARIFICATION, 5 candidates, all containing 'JK' as a distinctive token. 2) node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./lib/guided-research/orchestrator.ts').then(async(o)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify((await o.orchestrateGuidedResearch({action:{type:'START',question:'JK Moving Services'}})).result,null,2))})" from consumers-trust-hub -> resultState=SUPPORTED_RESULTS, total=34, displayed candidates include 'Ab Moving Services', 'Kings Moving Services', 'Bb&D Moving Services' with zero textual relation to 'JK'. Repeats with total=70 for 'Can JK Moving handle my move from Virginia to Florida?'. Control case 'AAA Moving' (many real matches) does NOT reproduce the leak -- all displayed rows stay AAA-prefixed on both contracts.
expected: Ask parent's displayed candidate set for a specific company-name search should not be materially broader or less name-relevant than the same specialist's own certified public contract for the identical input.
actual: For sparse-population name tokens (few real companies contain the token, e.g. 'JK'), the guided-research execution path (specialist-execution/v2) reports a total population an order of magnitude larger than the specialist's own move-ask-v1 contract, and surfaces candidates with no textual relation to the query.
violatedInvariant: "no huge unrelated name cohort" / "named company widened into unrelated cohort" (spec sections 9 and 22)
likelyCodeBoundary: lib/guided-research/specialists.ts executeMove() request/response handling is a thin pass-through (it does not itself broaden anything client-side -- verified by reading the function), so the widening most likely occurs server-side inside whatever backs POST https://www.movetrusthub.com/api/specialist-execution/v2. This is a SEPARATE contract from move-ask-v1 that R1-005's original hardening evidently never covered.
affectedPriorTickets: TH-SEARCH-R1-005 (certified conservative name-matching design that this defect violates)

TH-SEARCH-R1-016 (browser evidence for these exact two queries was reported as a working pass; this ticket's differential audit shows the underlying candidate set was already over-broad even though the top result was correct)
proposedR1018Scope: Investigate and fix the specialist-execution/v2 identity-name matching implementation (most likely in Move-trust-Hub) so that a sparse-population name query returns the same tight, distinctive-token-anchored candidate set as move-ask-v1, or -- if specialist-execution/v2 is intentionally a broader/fuzzier contract by design -- have the Ask parent apply its own client-side re-filtering against the requested name before display, and disclose the widening rather than presenting it silently as a plain 'X total matching records' count.

title: Insurance's guided-session block has no entity-name or geography extraction, defaulting nearly all natural insurance queries to an unscoped ~82,000-row agency cohort
owningRepoBestGuess: savitz25/Conumers-Trust-Hub -- confirmed by direct code reading, not inferred
exactReproduction: node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./lib/guided-research/session.ts').then(async(s)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(s.createGuidedSession('National Trust Insurance Group')))})" from consumers-trust-hub -> {hub:'insurance', insuranceResearchMode:'cohort', entityClass:'agency', identityName: undefined}. Same for createGuidedSession('insurance agencies in ZIP 33441') -> geography: undefined. Both then execute against specialist-execution/v2 and return total=82071 with candidates bearing no relation to the query.
expected: A specific company-name query should search by name; a ZIP-scoped query should filter by ZIP. Neither should fall back to the entire agency population.
actual: lib/guided-research/session.ts's insuranceIntent block (createUnscopedGuidedSession, ~lines 165-173) unconditionally sets insuranceResearchMode='cohort' whenever session.identifier is unset, with no identity-name extraction path at all (unlike lender/investor's 'named X' regex, and unlike Move post-R1-016), and does not parse ZIP/geography for the common phrasings tested here. The result: 82,071 total matching records for both a specific company-name search and a ZIP-scoped search.
violatedInvariant: "named company widened into unrelated cohort" / "important condition lost" / "silent geography broadening" (spec sections 8 EXACT IDENTIFIERS intent, 9/22 general widening prohibition)
affectedPriorTickets: None directly -- Insurance's guided-session block appears to have never had entity-name/geography extraction added, unlike the other five hubs which each have at least a partial mechanism
proposedR1018Scope: Add entity-name extraction (mirroring plan.entityName the way the R1-016 Move fix does) and geography/ZIP extraction (mirroring financialGeography as already computed and stored but apparently unused for insurance's own request-building) to lib/guided-research/session.ts's insurance block, and thread both into the specialist-execution/v2 request body the way lender/investor/move already do.

title: Labeled-identifier parsing captures a filler word ('code', 'number') instead of the actual value for natural phrasings like 'NAIC code 10064'
owningRepoBestGuess: savitz25/Conumers-Trust-Hub -- confirmed by direct code reading and live regex testing
exactReproduction: 'NAIC code 10064'.match(/\b(CRD|NPN|NAIC|NMLS|LEI)\s*#?\s*([A-Z0-9-]+)\b/i) -> ['NAIC code','NAIC','code']. Live confirmation: node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./lib/network/execution-decision.ts').then(async(ed)=>{const r=await(await import('./lib/guided-research/orchestrator.ts')).orchestrateGuidedResearch({action:{type:'START',question:'NAIC code 10064'}});console.log(JSON.stringify(r.result))})" -> resultState=INVALID_QUERY, 'NAIC Company Code must contain 3–5 digits.' The direct specialist (https://www.insurancetrusthub.com/api/ask?q=NAIC%20code%2010064) resolves the identical phrase correctly to CITIZENS PROP INS CORP.
expected: A natural, common phrasing like 'NAIC code 10064' (or 'NPN number 20000635', 'CRD number 166089', 'NMLS number 3030') should extract the real numeric value and resolve exactly, since the specialist itself proves the value is valid and resolvable.
actual: lib/guided-research/session.ts's labeledIdentifier regex greedily captures the word immediately following the label instead of skipping common filler words, corrupting the identifier value to the literal string 'code'/'number' before any specialist call is made, which is then correctly rejected as invalid by Ask's own downstream validation (the specialist never even sees the real request).
violatedInvariant: "common answerable query dead-ending despite acquired data" (spec section 22); exact identifier equality (sections 5, 8, 11)
likelyCodeBoundary: lib/guided-research/session.ts, the labeledIdentifier regex near the top of createUnscopedGuidedSession (~line 137)
affectedPriorTickets: None directly identified -- this looks like a long-standing latent defect in a regex that was likely only ever tested with the label immediately adjacent to the value (e.g. 'NAIC 10064'), not with a natural filler word
proposedR1018Scope: Fix the labeledIdentifier regex to skip common filler words ('code', 'company code', 'number', '#') between the label and the value, e.g. by matching the LAST alphanumeric run in the sentence after the label rather than the first token after whitespace. Re-verify end-to-end against NPN/CRD/NMLS 'number'-style phrasings in addition to the confirmed NAIC case, since the regex-level defect is identical for all five identifier families sharing this one parsing path.

title: A deictic reference to 'this nursing home' with no established facility identity gets the ENTIRE QUESTION TEXT captured as a fabricated literal facility name
owningRepoBestGuess: savitz25/Conumers-Trust-Hub -- confirmed by direct code reading
exactReproduction: node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./lib/network/execution-decision.ts').then(async(ed)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(ed.decideAskExecution('Who owns this nursing home?').plan.entityName))})" -> "Who owns this nursing home" (the entire question, not a real facility name). Reproduces identically for the paraphrase 'Can you tell me who owns this nursing home?' -> entityName = 'Can you tell me who owns this nursing home'.
expected: A deictic reference ('this nursing home') with no facility previously established in the conversation should trigger a missing-identity clarification, the same way 'this company'/'that facility' does for other hubs via DEICTIC_ENTITY.
actual: lib/network/research-planner.ts's DEICTIC_ENTITY regex lists 'facility' and 'home health agency' as deictic-reference triggers but not 'nursing home' (or 'assisted living facility', 'hospice'), so 'this nursing home' does not match DEICTIC_ENTITY. The query falls through to explicitEntityName()'s residue-fallback heuristic, which -- since entityClass=nursing_home was independently recognized and no geography is present -- strips only the class label from the question and keeps the >=2-word residue as a fabricated entity name, i.e. the whole question minus 'nursing home'.
violatedInvariant: "identity name extraction must not swallow whole questions" / R1-016 Bug #3 class defect recurring via a different regex gap; deictic-reference-requires-identity (spec section 12 facility-specific-evidence-requires-identity)
affectedPriorTickets: TH-SEARCH-R1-016 (Bug #3 fixed an analogous entity-name-extraction defect for Move; this is the same class of defect surfacing in a DEICTIC_ENTITY coverage gap for Senior)
proposedR1018Scope: Add 'nursing home', 'assisted living (facility)?', 'hospice', and 'senior (home|facility)' to the DEICTIC_ENTITY regex's noun list in research-planner.ts. Re-verify the fix does not regress SENIOR-OWNERSHIP-EXACT (which correctly resolves when a real CCN is present in the same phrasing) or the existing R1-008 senior test suite.

title: Contractor cohort-browse execution via the real production /ask page is completely non-functional due to a stale hardcoded contract version lock
owningRepoBestGuess: savitz25/Conumers-Trust-Hub -- confirmed by direct code reading and a live reproduction
exactReproduction: node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./lib/guided-research/orchestrator.ts').then(async(o)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify((await o.orchestrateGuidedResearch({action:{type:'START',question:'roofers in Broward County'}})).result))})" from consumers-trust-hub -> resultState=BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE, error.code='contract_version_mismatch', consumerMessage="ContractorTrustHub's structured research contract is temporarily unavailable because its version lock changed." Reproduces for every Contractor query in this corpus that reaches actual dispatch (3 of 3 attempted). Confirmed Contractor-specific: the same live check for Investor and Lender queries (which use a separate FINANCIAL_SPECIALIST_LOCKS mechanism) both still return SUPPORTED_RESULTS with no version-mismatch error.
expected: A well-formed, previously-certified Contractor cohort query (Broward roofers was already validated in R1-008/R1-016-era work) should execute successfully.
actual: Every Contractor cohort-browse query that reaches dispatch through the guided-research path fails immediately with a hard version-lock rejection, regardless of whether the underlying data or specialist behavior is otherwise fine.
violatedInvariant: "specialist fail_closed rendered as success" is avoided (this fails closed correctly, so it is at least not silently wrong) but violates "common answerable query dead-ending despite acquired data" (spec section 22) -- a complete functional outage, not a partial degradation.
likelyCodeBoundary: lib/guided-research/specialists.ts, lines 15-17 (CONTRACTOR_CONTRACT_VERSION/CONTRACTOR_SCHEMA_FINGERPRINT/CONTRACTOR_CONTRACT_FINGERPRINT hardcoded constants) and line 252 (the equality check against the live specialist response)
affectedPriorTickets: Any prior ticket that certified Contractor cohort-browse behavior via the guided-research path (R1-008, R1-009/010, R1-016's confirmation of the Broward/HVAC/typo-correction cases) should be considered potentially stale for the ask-execution surface specifically, though this sweep confirmed the underlying planner-level routing logic for those cases is still correct -- only the final specialist dispatch is blocked.
proposedR1018Scope: Update CONTRACTOR_CONTRACT_VERSION/CONTRACTOR_SCHEMA_FINGERPRINT/CONTRACTOR_CONTRACT_FINGERPRINT in lib/guided-research/specialists.ts to match the Contractor specialist's current live contract (coordinate with savitz25/contractor-trust-hub to confirm the current correct values), or replace the hard equality lock with the same compatible-version-acceptance pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase (see lib/network-metrics's 'a newer compatible contractRevision/sourceFingerprint is accepted without an Ask code change' pattern) so a future specialist-side version bump does not require a matching Ask parent deploy to avoid a full outage.

title: A two-domain request ('a mover and a mortgage lender in New Jersey') silently executes only one domain and discards the other with no disclosure
owningRepoBestGuess: savitz25/Conumers-Trust-Hub -- confirmed by direct code reading
exactReproduction: node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./lib/network/research-planner.ts').then(async(rp)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(rp.planAskResearch('I need a mover and a mortgage lender in New Jersey')))})" -> intent=COHORT_BROWSE (not MULTI_HUB_JOURNEY), candidateHubs=['lender','move'], primaryHub=undefined. Then node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./lib/guided-research/session.ts').then(async(s)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(s.createGuidedSession('I need a mover and a mortgage lender in New Jersey')))})" -> hub='lender', phase='EXECUTE' -- the lenderIntent early-return in createUnscopedGuidedSession claims the session before any multi-hub check. Full orchestrateGuidedResearch(START) confirms a real 776-row lender-only cohort is returned with no mention of the mover request. buildAskResearchRoute (a separate parent authorization surface) independently reports canExecute=false for the identical query -- the two layers disagree.
expected: Either a MULTI_HUB_JOURNEY hand-off preserving both requested domains, or an explicit clarification asking the user to pick one -- not a silent single-domain execution with the other request vanishing.
actual: research-planner.ts's MULTI_HUB_JOURNEY-detection regex requires the verb forms 'move'/'moving' and does not match the noun 'mover', so this 2-candidate-hub query never triggers MULTI_HUB_JOURNEY. Separately, lib/guided-research/session.ts evaluates hub-intent regexes in an early-return chain and the lenderIntent regex claims the session unconditionally once it matches, with no check for whether a second hub is also implicated.
violatedInvariant: "important condition lost" / "unrelated cohort filler" is avoided (the lender answer IS relevant) but the core violation is silent condition loss -- half the user's explicit request disappears with zero acknowledgment (spec section 22)
likelyCodeBoundary: lib/network/research-planner.ts's MULTI_HUB_JOURNEY regex (~line 245, missing the noun form 'mover'/'lender' alongside verb forms), and lib/guided-research/session.ts's early-return hub-intent chain in createUnscopedGuidedSession (investor/insurance/lender checks run before any multi-hub consideration)
affectedPriorTickets: None directly -- this appears to be a previously-untested combination (mover noun + lender in the same sentence); the existing MULTI_HUB_JOURNEY tests in the codebase use verb-form phrasings ('buying', 'moving') that happen to avoid this gap
proposedR1018Scope: Broaden the MULTI_HUB_JOURNEY trigger regex in research-planner.ts to include noun forms of hub-triggering terms (mover, lender, agent, contractor, adviser) when 2+ candidate hubs are present, not just verb forms (buying/moving/renting). Alternatively/additionally, have session.ts's early-return hub-intent chain check candidateHubs.length before committing to a single hub, and route to a clarification when multiple hubs are genuinely implicated and MULTI_HUB_JOURNEY wasn't already detected.
